issues.description: Constructor of Lucene99RWScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat calls super() which sets default 7-bit quantization, hiding the parameterized constructor's effect
issues.detail: The no-arg constructor delegates to super() while the parameterized one calls super(confidenceInterval, bits, compress). Tests using the parameterized form will work, but the no-arg constructor silently locks bits=7, which defeats testing other bit widths through default construction. State the invariant of which constructor the read/write tests rely on.

issues.description: Visibility downgrade of NAME constants from public to package-private may break external codec registration or reflection
issues.detail: Lucene99HnswScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat.NAME and Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat.NAME were public; they are now package-private. The SPI file references the class, but any external code (tests, tools, custom codec composition) referencing the NAME string by symbol will fail to compile. The invariant that NAME is a stable public identifier was broken silently.

issues.description: fieldsWriter throws UnsupportedOperationException but constructor still validates and stores write-only parameters
issues.detail: The Lucene99HnswScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat constructor validates maxConn, beamWidth, numMergeWorkers, and an executor service that is now unused (mergeExec/numMergeWorkers fields were removed). The IllegalArgumentException checks on numMergeWorkers and mergeExec are now dead constraints since writing throws unconditionally. State the invariant: this object is read-only; reject write-only parameters or remove the dead validation.

issues.description: Protected fields demoted to package-private on a public abstract class change the subclassing contract
issues.detail: OffHeapQuantizedByteVectorValues remains public and abstract, but its previously protected fields are now package-private. Any subclass outside this package (including downstream forks) loses access. If the intent is that no external subclasses exist, mark the class final or sealed; otherwise restore protected. The class-level invariant for subclassers is now ambiguous.

issues.description: Removal of @Deprecated annotation while moving to backward_codecs leaves deprecation signal weaker than the move warrants
issues.detail: The class was marked @Deprecated in core; after relocation to backward_codecs, the annotation was removed. Convention in this repo treats backward_codecs classes as legacy-by-package, but tooling and downstream IDEs still benefit from @Deprecated to flag usage at compile time. A literate comment stating 'read-only legacy; do not extend' would also help readers.

issues.description: calculateDefaultConfidenceInterval downgraded from public to package-private without documenting where callers were migrated
issues.detail: This was a public utility likely used outside the format class (e.g., by Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsWriter or external tooling). Downgrading visibility is fine only if all callers are inside the package. The PR should state the invariant: no external caller depends on this method. Otherwise extract to a small package-shared utility and document the migration.

review.summary: This is primarily a package-relocation and visibility-tightening PR — the algorithmic content of the scalar quantization formats is unchanged, so there are no invariants or complexity claims to re-audit. The work is largely RIGOROUS-by-relocation: the reader path is preserved, writing is intentionally disabled with UnsupportedOperationException, and an RW test shim restores write capability for tests. My concerns are NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT and contract clarity rather than correctness: visibility downgrades of NAME, calculateDefaultConfidenceInterval, and protected fields change public/subclass contracts silently; the write-only constructor parameters of the HNSW format are now dead weight; and the new RW test format's no-arg super() call obscures which bit width the tests actually exercise. None block merge, but the contract invariants deserve a one-line comment each before this lands.
